blocks.content:
Bills introduced in State Legislature may be:
• Ordinary Bills
• Money Bills

Money Bill:
• Introduced only in Legislative Assembly
• Requires prior recommendation of Governor
• Legislative Council can only make recommendations

rows: Exclusive house for introduction of Money Bills

items: Money Bills CANNOT be introduced in the Legislative Council; origin is restricted solely to the Legislative Assembly.
Introduction of a Money Bill always requires the prior recommendation of the Governor.
The Legislative Council cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; its authority is restricted to making recommendations.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Bills introduced in the State Legislature are categorized into Ordinary Bills and Money Bills.
Money Bills can be introduced strictly in the Legislative Assembly only.
The prior recommendation of the Governor is mandatory for introducing a Money Bill.
The Legislative Council holds limited power over Money Bills and can only offer recommendations.
